title: Withholding Shares on a Keyturn Host Payout Account Where Tax Documentation is Missing
content:
The share withheld from a draw on a Keyturn Host Payout Account for tax documentation turns on the state of that documentation and on what the account has earned.

1. **Where the tax documentation on the account is not on file and the earnings credited to it in the twelve months up to that day stand above the documentation threshold of 600.00 USD**, the full withholding share of 24 percent applies.
2. **Where the tax documentation on the account is not on file and the earnings credited to it in that period stand at or below 600.00 USD**, the reduced withholding share of 10 percent applies.
3. **In every other case**, nothing is withheld, the share standing at 0 percent.

The share is taken on the payable balance, and the sum withheld is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## The threshold, from both sides

Earnings of exactly 600.00 USD in the twelve months up to that day stand at the threshold rather than above it, so an account whose documentation is not on file and whose earnings come to 600.00 USD falls in the second case at 10 percent. At 600.01 USD the first case governs at 24 percent.

## Where the documentation is on file

Both of the first two cases require that the documentation is not on file. An account whose tax documentation is on file falls in the third case whatever it has earned, and nothing is withheld from it.

## On hypothetical figures

Where the payable balance is 4000.00 USD, the sum withheld is 960.00 USD in the first case, 400.00 USD in the second and 0.00 USD in the third.

The state of the documentation is carried on the account's own record, and the earnings are the earning entries credited to the account in the twelve months up to that day.
